edges.label: Friedman's February 1978 interview reopened Roswell
edges.note: Friedman was put in touch with the retired Lt. Col. Marcel in Baton Rouge and obtained his statement that the weather balloon account was a cover. Attested by Friedman on the record and repeated by Marcel in filmed interviews.

edges.label: Unresolved dispute over MJ-12 authenticity
edges.note: Friedman held there were no substantive grounds for dismissing the core documents while himself proving parts of the corpus faked; Randle concluded the whole was not authentic. Neither position has been settled by any released record.

edges.label: Moore's 1989 AFOSI admission is Randle's strongest argument against MJ-12
edges.note: Moore stated publicly at the 1989 MUFON symposium that he had cooperated with AFOSI and passed disinformation to Paul Bennewitz; Randle's 'Conclusions on Operation Majestic Twelve' (1994) and 'Case MJ-12' (2002) treat the corpus as fabricated.

edges.label: Made the AFOSI disinformation admission from the MUFON platform
edges.note: Moore chose the 1989 MUFON symposium in Las Vegas to state that he had cooperated with Air Force Office of Special Investigations personnel and passed disinformation to Paul Bennewitz.

edges.label: Moore and Shandera's 1984 film delivery became Friedman's decade-long project
edges.note: Friedman became aware of the MJ-12 documents through Moore and Jaime Shandera in 1984 and defended their core authenticity through 'Top Secret/Majic' (1996).
